title: Microsoft Patch Tuesday for November 2026 — Snort rules and prominent vulnerabilities
content_md: Microsoft has released its monthly security update for November 2026, which includes 1095 vulnerabilities affecting a range of products, including 64 that Microsoft marked as "critical." Microsoft notes that 1 of the vulnerabilities disclosed this month have been exploited in the wild CVE-2026-124194 affects Microsoft Office Outlook. CVE-2026-124194 is a spoofing vulnerability involving Product UI does not Warn User of Unsafe Actions and has a CVSS base score of 6.5. Out of 64 "critical" vulnerabilities, 48 are remote code execution (RCE) vulnerabilities. Microsoft considers exploitation of the following vulnerabilities more likely: CVE-2026-113862 affects Windows Network Address Translation (NAT). CVE-2026-113862 is a remote code execution vulnerability involving Use After Free and has a CVSS base score of 8.1. CVE-2026-118146 and CVE-2026-118148 affect Active Directory Domain Services. CVE-2026-118146 is a remote code execution vulnerability involving Incorrect Authorization and has a CVSS base score of 8.8. CVE-2026-118148 is an elevation of privilege vulnerability involving Incorrect Authorization and has a CVSS base score of 7.5. CVE-2026-118207 affects Microsoft Exchange Server. CVE-2026-118207 is a remote code execution vulnerability involving Use of Incorrectly-Resolved Name or Reference and has a CVSS base score of 8.8. CVE-2026-119952 affects Windows Schannel.
